# Quietbox 2 user experience notes

## Round 1

- Got a vsix file (VSCode extension file) from Taylor of the latest version of the extension.  
- Installed VSCode from Ubuntu App Center  
- Installed the extension in VSCode via the ctrl-shift-p “Install Extension from VSIX command  
- ![][image1]  
- Process was quick and smooth, installing all the dependencies needed and popping open a pretty “Welcome to Tenstorrent” starting point.   
- I skipped the first step since I have a QuietBox  
- ![][image2]  
- Moved on to “Hardware Detection” the first step in the “Your First Inference” learning path  
- I skipped right to running `tt-smi` since I have a QB with preinstalled image, it worked right away.  
  - 🚩 Noticed that my card type (p300c) is not “Validated” in the lesson header  
  - “Expected Output” section does not show a reference for p300c cards either  
  - As I scrolled further down the page past the debugging steps (didn’t need them since everything was working A-OK) I noticed there is a section for QuietBox Multi-Device systems  
  - Seeing “P100” when I have “P300c” is confusing. Is this correct?  
- Feeling confident I know what is running next to me, I clicked the next step button “Verify tt-metal Installation” but got a “Lesson not found” error, so I tabbed back to the starting page and selected that lesson manually

- “Run the Verification”

  ![][image5]

## Round 4

- Deleted everything, started from scratch again but this time **forcing docker instead of podman** via tt-installer. Logged this for June as it seems to be causing issues for others as well: [DEVSTACK-42: ISO - Switch tt-installer to use Docker by default instead of Podman](https://tenstorrent.atlassian.net/browse/DEVSTACK-42)

### Verify tt-metal installation

- Went through docs, having a much better time. Noticed that the pre-baked tt-installer creates a tenstorrent virtual environment that gets activated when \~/.bashrc is sourced. Perhaps we can update the extension to warn about this

```
(python_env_3.12) ttuser@tt-quietbox:~/tt-metal$ 
echo 'export TT_METAL_HOME=~/tt-metal' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export PYTHONPATH=$TT_METAL_HOME:$PYTHONPATH' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/openmpi-v5.0.7-ulfm/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc(.tenstorrent-venv) ttuser@tt-quietbox:~/tt-metal$ 


```

- **Build from source working\! Excellent\!**  
- Note: “When to use Which” section came *after* I had already installed from source, it would be beneficial to have this up front so I can choose beforehand if I just want to run inference

- Same error. **Glean**’d it

```py
mesh_device = ttnn.open_mesh_device(
  ttnn.MeshShape(1, len(ttnn.get_device_ids())),
  dispatch_core_config=ttnn.DispatchCoreConfig(ttnn.DispatchCoreType.WORKER, ttnn.DispatchCoreAxis.ROW),

-->
mesh_device = ttnn.open_mesh_device(
  ttnn.MeshShape(1, 1),
  dispatch_core_config=ttnn.DispatchCoreConfig(ttnn.DispatchCoreType.WORKER),
)



logits = generator.decode_forward_text(
-->
logits = generator.decode_forward(
```

- This got me slightly further, but then got another error: ❌ Error generating response: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'unsqueeze'  
- Glean said: *decode\_forward on your tt-metal version is already doing the right thing and, with sampling\_params set, returns a tuple (tokens / logits, maybe logprobs), not a bare tensor. The template’s .unsqueeze(1) assumed a tensor, hence 'tuple' object has no attribute 'unsqueeze'. Simplest fix: turn off on-device sampling and always do sampling on host.*  
  - At this point, I decided to move on to the next lesson
